If you’re still holding expiring quarterly futures without a rollover plan, stop now.

A lot of traders learn this the hard way. Contracts expire, liquidity shifts, and suddenly you’re scrambling to close or reopen positions while the market moves against you. Missing that transition window has cost traders real money.

Binance Futures just confirmed that new USDⓈ-M and COIN-M Quarterly 1225 delivery contracts will go live shortly after the current 0626 contracts expire and settle at 08:00 UTC on June 26, 2026. The new lineup includes BTCUSDT and ETHUSDT quarterly contracts settled in USDT, with tick sizes of 0.1 for $BTC and 0.01 for $ETH.

Some traders love quarterly futures because they remove funding fees and make longer-term positioning cleaner. Others argue they’re a trap for overleveraged traders who forget expiration risk and get forced into messy rollovers. Both sides have a point, especially when volatility spikes around settlement windows.

Do you think quarterly futures like these make trading $BTC and $ETH safer for structured positions, or do they just add another way for traders to get caught off guard?
